deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building a 2-dimensional cell complex (the surface 𝔛, or Σ) attached to a system of pseudo-lines in the projective plane X. Each line D of the system contributes a disc Δ_D. When D specializes to D' (crosses a critical line or crossing δ), two discs Δ_D and Δ_{D'} are glued along a transition arc b. The resulting surface should map naturally to X, ideally by an immersion. Two choices are on the table: which arc on ∂Δ_{D'} represents the generalization D'→D (α = a' or α = a), and which isomorphism relates the orientations of Δ_D and Δ_{D'}. An orientation of Δ_D is determined by an orientation ω_D of D.

First paragraph. He ends the discussion of the previous page's choice α = a' by noting a defect. With the other gluings, the 'holes' (and the vertices on their boundaries) of the glued complex seem to have no interpretation in terms of the geometry of Σ. He decides to re-check whether he has 'got his brushes tangled'.

His finding: suppose one glues so that an orientation ω of Δ_D (from ω_D) continues across the transition arc into an orientation ω' of Δ_{D'}. Then ω' induces on D' the orientation OPPOSITE to the one obtained from ω_D by parallel transport along the specialization. He calls this a (monumental?) error committed 'in the beginnings': earlier he had used parallel transport as the transition isomorphism for orientations.

Second column. He examines the other choice, α = a, which also gives a map 𝔛→X. As announced on the previous page, the discs must be shrunk to Δ_D^*, Δ_{D'}^*, with b moved to b^* and a to a^*, so that b and a meet in b^*∩a^* ⊂ X.

The figure shows the local picture:
- two (orange) lines crossing;
- the critical line of specialization δ (dotted, with a thick segment at the crossing);
- a hatched strip on one bank of δ;
- the orientations ω_D, ω_{D'} (the latter curving back, reversed), and ω' = ω.

Interpretation: with this choice one glues the same bank of the strip along δ to itself, via the identification b^*→a^* and the transport isomorphism. He then starts to list the combinations: choice of polygonal structures on the set of associated transitions, one per..., versus the opposite choice. The next page completes this into a list of four possibilities. Again ω_{D'} turns out opposite to the parallel transport of ω_D.

Mathematically, this is a careful sign and orientation bookkeeping in a gluing construction. The orientation reversal relative to naive parallel transport reflects the twisting of lines and pencils in RP^2 (the space of lines is a Möbius band / RP^2).
errors: Grothendieck himself flags an earlier error: he had taken parallel transport as the transition isomorphism for orientations and the wrong (parallel-transported rather than antipodal/'facing') arc for the generalization. This page records the correction.
The page is exploratory and incomplete. The final classification of gluings is deferred to the next page, and no claim about the global structure (immersion, interpretation of holes) is proved here.

ideas.what: Surface obtained by gluing discs Δ_D (one per pseudo-line) along transition arcs indexed by specializations D→D', with a map to the projective plane X
ideas.modern_name: cell complex / dual surface of a pseudoline arrangement; related to zonotopal tilings and the cell structure of oriented-matroid realization/mutation spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: pseudoline arrangements: Levi (1926), Ringel (1956), Goodman–Pollack (1980s), Folkman–Lawrence (1978) for the topological representation

ideas.what: Orientation transition across a specialization is the opposite of parallel transport
ideas.modern_name: orientation-character / local-system sign in a non-orientable gluing (w_1 twist of the tautological line over the space of lines)

ideas.what: Choice of the bank of a critical line of specialization δ (arc 'facing' vs. parallel-transported arc) to represent a generalization
ideas.modern_name: choice of local model at a mutation / flip in an arrangement

missed.claim: Grothendieck's whole program on 'systems of pseudo-lines' builds a surface from discs indexed by lines, glued along specialization arcs and mapping to the plane. It remains unpublished and was never compared with the oriented-matroid literature (Folkman–Lawrence, Goodman–Pollack, Mnëv). This page is a technical step (orientation conventions) in that unfinished construction, not a result in itself.
missed.quote: on n'ait aucune interprétation des "trous" (ou sommets, qui sont au bord des trous) en termes de la géométrie de Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The question of interpreting the holes and vertices of the glued complex in terms of Σ is a concrete open thread. It could be checked against known cell structures, e.g. the Salvetti complex, zonotopal tilings, or higher Bruhat orders.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a self-correction of orientation and gluing conventions in an exploratory construction. It interests historians (the record of an early error and two weeks of work on the gluing), but contains no finished result or new connection.
transcription_corrections: 'vérifiée une erreur nouvelle' — the image looks more like 'une erreur monumentale, commise dans les débuts !'
'si je n'étais pas mélangé les pinceaux' — idiom 's'emmêler les pinceaux' ('si je ne m'étais pas emmêlé les pinceaux'), consistent with the next page.
'Voyons-un : l'autre choix' — probably 'Voyons aussi/maintenant l'autre choix qui donne lieu à 𝔛 → X'.
'qui est opposée par parallélité' — sense is 'opposée à celle déduite de ω_D par transport parallèle' (parallélisme).
'ou les autres se obtiennent' — likely 'où les autres s'obtiennent par recollement'.
Label in figure: ω_{D'} (dark green curve, arrow reversed) and ω' = ω above the hatching; δ is the critical line of specialization.
